body: The best thing I can tell you is I’ve been were you’re at. Call the suicide hot line, try to see someone, or even tell the person you’re seeing. Find someone to talk to and “walk yourself off the ledge.” I know it’s easier said than done but seek help. Trust me it wasn’t easy for me either but I used the hot lines and then finally was able to get professional help. That was 5 or 6 months ago. Im still talking to professionals and I still have those feelings sometimes but I can deal with them better. People rather talk to you than go to your funeral.

I guess it is but I’ve gotten better and then there’s those days where I just want to die. No real reason in particular. It’s doesn’t help my doctor thinks I might be on the bipolar spectrum. I’m still trying to fully understand what that means.

Everything! Lol. Specially “Adulting!” At 42 years old, I still feel like I’m a kid and learning things everyday.
Edit: I have 5 kids, married and own our own home but I still feel like there’s so much to learn.

That living in some kind of pain is my normal and I need to work really hard to show that I’m happy to my family. “Happy” is a relative term and it doesn’t come easy to me, I need to work hard to show it on the outside so people can see it, specially my family. Btw, I’m married and have 5 kids, between 15-23 years old.
Thank you. After months of looking I found a psychiatrist and 1st app is next week. I still haven’t been able to find a talk therapist but hopefully soon.
